About CUSB
Central University of South Bihar, Gaya, India,
is one among 54 such universities of Federal Government, which come under the purview of the Department of Higher Education under the Ministry of Education of Government of India.
It was established under the Central Universities Act, 2009 (Section 25 of 2009) as Central University of Bihar (CUB) and the name since changed by the Central Universities (Amendment) Act, 2014 to Central University of South Bihar (CUSB).
It is an institution of higher learning in the state of Bihar. With the motto, i.e. ‘Collective Reasoning’ the University has been conducting its academic and administrative activities from permanent campus on a 300 acre plot of land at Panchanpur, situated about 15 kms away from Gaya town.
The University welcomes all with a grand Entrance Plaza and further provides visual delight with a half-globe shaped Stupa and a magnificent multi-storied Administrative Block building. Besides, the massive Schools buildings namely School of Earth, Biological & Environmental Sciences named as Aryabhatta Bhawan, School of Social Sciences & Policy named as Chanakya Bhawan,
School of Education
building named as Malaviya Bhawan, Vivekanand Lecture Complex, Sangharam Guest House, Boys Hostel named as Gargi Sadan and Girls Hostel named as Maitreyi Sadan altogether are like visual treat for visitors, and offering a pristine environs for running academic and co-curricular activities. Along with world-class highly qualified faculty members, high teacher-student ratio, baskets full of elective courses in different programmes, the University offers Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) with total internal evaluation of students’ performance at Undergraduate (UG) and Postgraduate (PG) levels. Other highlights of CUSB includes a conducive and research oriented environment with multidisciplinary approach, innovative pedagogies, promising infrastructural facilities and effective students’ support system to nurture students’ personality in a holistic manner and to prepare them for bright future.
The University’s academic programme started functioning with a rented building in the premises of Birla Institute of Technology, Patna (BIT) in 2009. The zeal and enthusiasm among the administration, faculty, staff and students helped the university to move ahead in the desired direction in the field of higher studies. The academic journey of (the) university began with the Centre for Development Studies (under the School of Social Sciences & Policy), and a (two) 2-year Master of Arts in Development Studies was launched in the academic year 2009-10 at the BIT campus.
Campus Address :
SH-7, Gaya Panchanpur Road, Village – Karhara, Post. Fatehpur, Gaya – 824236 (Bihar)

Central Universities Act, 2009
Central University Act, 2009 was passed by the Parliament in the 60th year of the Republic of India, which aims to establish universities directly governed by the federal government for teaching and research purposes, across all the States in India. The Central University of Bihar (CUB) is one amongst the 16 new Central Universities, established by the Government of India under the Central Universities Act, 2009 (Section 25 of 2009).
Subsequently, the name of the university was changed by the Central Universities (Amendment) Act, 2014 to Central University of South Bihar (CUSB).

History and Development
Milestones
First Vice-Chancellor :
Prof. Janak Pandey, joined on March 2, 2009
Started functioning from :
Hindi Bhawan, Patna
Started Academic Session :
On 1st September, 2009, with the PG Programme in Development Studies
First Convocation held on 26th September, 2013 (Thursday) :
The First Convocation was graced by Hon’ble Shri M. Hamid Ansari, Vice President of India as Chief Guest. Hon’ble Smt. Meira Kumar, Chancellor of the University and Speaker, Lok Sabha attended the convocation along with the Chief Minister of Bihar, Hon’ble Nitish Kumar; the Education Minister of Government of Bihar, Hon’ble Shri P. K. Shahi; and many other distinguished guests. A total of 156 graduates of the first three batches since the inception of CUB in 2009 were awarded the Degrees by the dignitaries.
The Central University of Bihar (CUB),
is one amongst the 16 new Central Universities established by the Government of India under the Central Universities Act, 2009 (Section 25 of 2009). The first Vice-Chancellor Prof. Janak Pandey joined on 2nd March, 2009 and started functioning from a single room at Hindi Bhawan in Patna. Since then the University has made a steady progress in terms of academic achievements; the numbers of courses being taught; faculty; staff members; computer lab; media lab; science labs; and equipping the classrooms for e-learning.
The University began its academic activities with the MA Programme in Development Studies in 2009. Till date, the university has been able to offer four (4) Integrated undergraduate (UG) programmes, 25 postgraduate (PG) programmes and 22 Ph.D. programmes. The campus of the University is spread over about 300 acres of land located on Gaya-Panchanpur Road, about 15 kms away from Gaya Railway Station.
2009 – 10 :
The University made its beginning by establishing the Centre for Development Studies under the
School of Social Sciences and Policy
, and launched its first PG Programme.
2010 – 11 :
Five more PG Programmes in, viz., Biotechnology, Computer Science, Environmental Sciences, Mathematics, and Statistics were launched.
2011 – 12 :
Three more PG Programmes, viz., Bioinformatics, Communication and Media Studies, and Psychology were added.
2012 – 13 :
Seven more PG Programmes started, viz., Life Science, Economics, English, Hindi, Political Science and International Relations, Sociology, and MTech in Computer Science.
2013 – 14 :
Integrated BA. BEd; Integrated BSc. BEd; Integrated BA. LLB (Hons); Integrated BSc. LLB (Hons); and Integrated M.Phil-Ph.D. Programme in Bioinformatics, Biotechnology, Computer Science, Development Studies, Economics, Environmental Science, Hindi, Life Science, Mathematics, Political Science & International Relations and Statistics were introduced. (Integrated MPhil – PhD was replaced with PhD programme w.e.f. Academic Year 2016-17)
2014 – 15 :
B.Voc (Arts & Crafts) has been introduced under School of Vocational Studies from 2015-16 academic session (# the course was withdrawn w.e.f. from 2017-18 Academic session due to technical reasons).
2016 – 17 :
The University introduced LLM programme under School of Law Governance from the Academic Year 2016-17. In addition, Ph.D. programmes in all Centres / Departments were introduced in accordance with the UGC (Minimum Standard and Procedure for Award of M.Phil / Ph.D. Degree) Regulations, 2016. Ph.D. programme was started in 16 departments /centres viz. (i) Biotechnology (ii) Life Science (iii) Environmental Science (iv) Mathematics (v) Statistics (vi) Communication and Media Studies (vii) Psychology (viii) Computer Science (ix) Hindi (x) English (xi) Sociology (xii) Development Studies (xiii) Economics (xiv) Political Science & International Relations (xv) Education and (xvi) Law and (xvii) Bioinformatics
2017 – 18 :
M.Ed. programme was introduced by the University during the Academic Year 2017-18 under Department of Teacher Education.
2018 – 19 :
From the Academic Session 2018-19, the University started five (5) new Postgraduate (PG) programmes in five subjects namely, Chemistry, Physics, Social Work, M.Com and History under Dept. of Chemistry, Physics, Sociological Studies, Commerce & Business Studies and Historical Studies & Archaeology respectively.
2019 – 20 :
The University introduced Ph.D. programme during the academic year 2019-20 under Department of Chemistry, School of Physical and Chemical Sciences.

Milestones
Bhoomi Pujan of the Campus Land on 27th February, 2014 (Thursday) : The University Chancellor and Lok Sabha Speaker, Hon’ble Smt. Meira Kumar laid down the foundation stone at the 300-acre campus-site amidst great enthusiasm and fervour in Panchanpur, in the district of Gaya in Bihar. Hon’ble Shri P. K. Shahi, Education Minister of Bihar was present as distinguished guest on the occasion along with Shri Sushil Kumar Singh, Member of Parliament, Aurangabad; Shri Hari Manjhi, Member of Parliament, Gaya; and, Dr. Anil Kumar, Member of the Legislative Assembly Tikari. Prof. Janak Pandey, Vice-Chancellor was present on the occasion along with the other members of the Executive Council, Pro-Vice Chancellor Prof. Debdas Banerjee, Registrar Prof. Mohammad Nehal, faculty, officers, staff and students. A large number of people from the neighbouring areas and other parts of Bihar gathered at the CUB’s upcoming campus to witness the grand celebration.
CUBET (Central University of Bihar Entrance Test) 2014 :
For the first time the University successfully conducted the online entrance test CUBET (Central University of Bihar Entrance Test) on May 30 & 31, 2014. The entrance test was held for admission to undergraduate, postgraduate and Integrated MPhil-PhD programmes offered by the university for academic session 2014-15. A total of 2127 candidates appeared in the online test conducted at 15 different centres across the country including Bihar and other states
Foundation Laying of Buildings on 31st August, 2015 :
Union HRD minister Smt. Smriti Zubin Irani laid down the foundation stone at the 300-acre campus-site in presence of CUSB Vice-Chancellor Prof. Harish Chandra Singh Rathore and entire university fraternity. The minister was accompanied by people from politicians namely, Ram Kumar Sharma, Member of Parliament, MLC Krishna Kumar Singh, Dr. Anil Kumar, Member of Legislative Assembly from Tikari (Gaya), Vinay Sheel Oberoi, Secretary, Dept of Higher Education among many others on the dais. The Union minister laid the foundation of seven buildings of CUSB under first Phase, namely, Central Office, Schools of Earth, Biological & Environmental Sciences, School of Social Sciences & Policy, Boys Hostel, Girls Hostel, Lecture complex and dining hall.
Accreditation from AICTE :
The University received the recognition from AICTE (All India Council for Technical Education) to offer the ongoing M.Tech in Computer Science programme in 2015.
Accreditation from NCTE :

Accreditation from BCI :

Grade ‘A’ NAAC Accreditation :
CUSB was accredited with ‘A’ grade by NAAC (National Assessment and Accreditation Council) in its first attempt itself on 25th May, 2016.
2nd Vice-Chancellor of CUSB – 05th August 2015 :
Prof. H.C.S. Rathore Assumed Charge as 2nd Vice-Chancellor of CUSB. Prof. Rathore has a very vast and impressive academic as well as administrative experience. Before joining CUSB, Prof Rathore was the Dean of Faculty of Education at Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Varanasi. He was also the co-ordinator of Internal Quality Assurance Cell of BHU. He has received many fellowships for his praiseworthy contribution to the field of Education. Prof. Rathore has received many awards and recognitions for his work. DAAD, Humbolt Fellowship, etc. are among the renowned fellowships received by Prof. Rathore. Prof. Rathore is also having good administrative experience. He had been the Chief Proctor of BHU for the period of about six years, which is the longest for any Proctor in the University. A senior professor, Prof. Rathore is member of several national committees constituted by MHRD, UGC, NAAC and NCTE. In addition to these, he is having membership of more than a dozen professional national and international bodies.
94th Rank in NIRF Ranking – 2016 :
In the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) ranking, CUSB was listed among top 100 Universities of India, which was declared by Ministry of Human Resource Development, Govt. of India on 4th April, 2016. By securing the 94th position, CUSB became the only University in Bihar to find a place in NIRF Ranking and also remained at top position among the Universities in the state.

Salient Features and Best Practices
1. Current Academic Programmes :
Presently the University offers three (3) Undergraduate (UG) programmes, 25 Postgraduate (PG) programmes and 22 Ph.D. programmes through 25 departments under 11 schools.
2. Semester System :
Semester system is followed in all of the academic programmes in order to enlarge curricular space and encourage more learning opportunities. Moreover, the latter enhances the ability to accommodate diverse choices that dynamic and motivated students may like to have. The decisions regarding faculty-to-students contact hours during a semester in different programmes; the decision regarding the credit system determining the quantum of class room learning hours; elements of participatory teaching-learning process; field-work; lab-work; and, other curricular work are taken by various academic bodies of the university.
3. Choice-Based Credit System (CBCS) :
It has some unique features, such as enhanced learning opportunities, ability to match student’s scholastic needs and aspirations, horizontal intra-, and inter-School/ Centre mobility of students, inter-institutional transferability of students, improvement in educational quality and excellence, flexibility for working students to complete the programme over an extended period of time, innovation and comparability of educational programmes across the country. CBCS will facilitate vertical integration of knowledge and holistic development of self.
4. Evaluation System :
‘Continuous Internal Evaluation’ is the central feature of the evaluation system in this university. A teacher who offers the course is the best person to assess performance of the students. However, there is the end-semester evaluation. And, to ensure transparency, fairness, and accountability appropriate mechanisms have been devised.
5. Infrastructure and ambience :
All appropriate steps are taken to create and maintain infrastructure required for quality teaching and research.
6. Governance & E-Governance :
The University has been evolving dynamic, transparent, equal-opportunity governance, and need based capacity-building system. The University is following a decentralised and participative system of governance to achieve the mandate stated in the Act and Statues. Faculty members are directly involved in decision-making bodies of the University, which in turn helps the students in a great way for redressal of their grievances. Each department of the University has a Departmental Committee and it takes the decisions for academic proposals at initial state before being placed before Apex decision-making bodies of the University. The Board of Studies (BOS) is also an important body of the department which specifically looks after the curriculum development work. Also, the University has put it efforts towards the use of E-Governance tools to bring effectiveness into its administration to promote transparency and efficiency in the system. : It had been moving towards e-governance and continuous training of the personnel to make the university system ‘user-friendly’. Professional enrichment of education administrators would become a necessary component for the capacity building of the university administration.
7. Psychological Counselling and Guidance Services:
Like physical health, mental health determines efficiency and productivity. Mental health is critically important to teaching-learning processes, creativity and congenial environment in academic institutions. The university adopts a forward looking approach and provides psychological counselling and guidance services to the students, faculty and employees. Innovative programmes, such as ‘Crises Intervention Programmes’ and ‘Community Mental Health Programme’ are planned to be developed.
8. Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation:
The University is having an Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC) to ensure progressive improvement in efficiency of the functioning of the institution specifically the University administration. The Planning, Development and Monitoring Board (PDMB) with appropriate powers and functions is instituted following UGC guidelines.
9. Admission and its National Character:
UGC guidelines are followed in the university admission process. Efforts are made to have students from all over the country. And, to achieving the same, the Admission to various programmes (courses) of the University is made through national level entrance test jointly conducted by 14 Central Universities and named as Central Universities Common Entrance Test (CUCET). With its transparent and national level admission process, the University has succeeded to attract the students from different states and maintaining the diversity and national character efficiently.
10. Scholarship Schemes:
All research scholars (Ph.D.) students get UGC scholarship. In addition to Centre government and state government funded scholarships, the University offers a number of scholarship schemes to deserving and needy students, namely (i) Merit Scholarship to CUSBET / Semester Toppers (ii) Merit-cum-Means Scholarship (iii) Earn While You Learn (EWYL) Scheme & (iv) Attendance Based Merit Scholarship.
11 . Hostels for Accommodation:
Presently the University offers accommodation to students with one (1) Boys Hostel and one (1) Girls Hostel having combined capacity to accommodate around 800 students. Mess facility is also available for students residing in the hostels on payment basis.
12 . Health Centre / Medical Facility:
The University has its Health Centre, which provides primary level treatment to faculty, staff and students for general ailments under the supervision of Medical officer.
13. Vidyarthi Mediclaim Policy:
All the students of the University are insured under this scheme. This is a unique policy of National Insurance Company (NIC) designed to provide health and personal accident cover to the students. Under this scheme the students are eligible for cashless treatment in authorized hospitals as well as for reimbursement of cost of treatment in other hospitals within the limit of Rs. 50,000.
14. Campus Placement:
The University has a Career Counselling and Placement Cell which takes care of the campus placements and job opportunities for the students. Many students got job placement during the session 2018 – 19 in organisations like Azim Premji Foundation, Care India (NGO), Gandhi Fellowship – Piramal Foundation, etc. Students from Media department got placements in Times of India, Hindustan Times, ETV Bharat, Hindustan Dainik and Prabhat Khabar and along with many other organisations.
15. Internships:
Keeping in view the importance of role of practice based learning / first-hand industry experience the University makes arrangements for internship opportunities to the students during Summer vacation.
16. Sports & Cultural / Co-curricular Activities:
The University has committees like Games and Sports Activities Committee, Cultural Activities Committee which conducts various activities for students round the year. The students of the University participate in the state and nation level competitions and events under the supervision of co-ordinators of the committees and impress all with their brilliant performances.
17. Proctorial Board:
The board is responsible to maintain discipline among the students of University and it functions under supervision of the Chief Proctor. The Proctorial board takes preventive steps to maintain the discipline within the University premises, issues the notices and warnings as per need of the situation.
18. Student Welfare Board:
The Dean Students’ Welfare (DSW) is shouldering the responsibility of looking after the general welfare of students outside classrooms, in order to ensure all round development. The office of DSW also performs the duties and functions viz. (i) make arrangements for educational tours, excursions and participation in sports activities outside the University (ii) conduct social and cultural activities (iii) form of student bodies (iv) evaluate student – teacher relationship (v) examine and recommend for financial aid to needy students and concession for travel, and other facilities (vi) facilitate fellowships / scholarships for further studies in the country or abroad (vii) student counselling (viii) provide special assistance (if required) to differently abled students or women students (ix) provide Student information services (x) organise alumni association (xii) issue certificates as authorised and delegated by the Vice-Chancellor.
Best Practices
1. Zero Water Discharge
Elaborate arrangement has been made to ensure that the water discharged through sewerage
gets recycled. The rain water is collected in the artificially constructed ponds located at the north-east of the campus through a network of drainage system.
2. Planned Waste Disposal
University has well defined protocol for all types of hazardous, chemical and other waste disposal.
3. Student Involvement in Community Development
Students are engaged in the local community development either through non-credit courses as a part of their curriculums e.g. courses like  Village-based Skills, Plantation of Trees, or students are encouraged and motivated to participate in such activities. One such successful student-driven organization within the CUSB is SMiLE group which has been actively involved in helping surrounding unprivileged children by distributing stationary and other essential items and also helping them learn the subjects.

University Kulgeet
The University Kulgeet was Composed by Dr. Hari Prasad Dubey in 2013. At the First Convocation of CUSB on 26 September 2013, it was sung in its fine musical form by singers-team led by Dr. Richa Vatsa (CUSB) with esteemed musicians (Late) Prof. R. P. Shastri (BHU) on Violin, Dr. Vijay Kapoor (BHU) on Harmonium, and Mr. Raj Shekhar (DPS, Patna) on Tabla. This can be played online and downloaded from the link given at the end of this page.
Genesis of University Kulgeet
The credos of Kulgeet (University Anthem) of Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) are nature, environment, compassion and cultural consciousness of the historical land of Bihar. The poet has penned it down keeping in mind the world famous rich cultural heritage of the glorious land of Bihar. While writing the poet has taken inspirations from the Holy City of Gaya, the land of salvation, which is also referred as the Tapobhoomi of Mahatma Buddha, Pitritirtha and Vishnu Nagar. Elevating the standards of life and making it beautiful is the prime goal of Human life. Vidhaiva Sarvam is the motto of life and service to humanity is like a precious immortal gift. Simplicity, values and generosity also make character of Human being great. In the Kulgeet the poet has dreamed of making India a Vishwaguru by disseminating quality education with cultural and human values. To build India’s future, all types of difficulties coming on the way must be surpassed by promising hard work. Persistent efforts with the honest intention can make the great History that is achievable as the Kulgeet describes Bihar as the culturally rich land of all religious faiths. How to Reach CUSB
The CUSB Gaya campus is located on SH-7 Gaya-Panchanpur road, around 15 Kms from Gaya Railway Station and 25 Kms from Gaya Airport. The campus is well connected through air, railway and road. It is about 15 km from Gaya Railway station. Gaya Railway station is on the main line of the Eastern railway from Howrah to Delhi, which is 20 km from Gaya International Airport and 98 km from Patna airport.
Globally known as an abode of Bhagwan Gautam Buddha, Gaya is a famous destination for Buddhist pilgrimage as well as Holy locations for Hindus. Devotees and tourists throng the city of Gaya round the year for paying a visit to Bodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya, while the Hindus visit the city for the religious ritual of ‘Pindaan’ – a special puja for salvation of their ancestors. Over the years, Gaya, the southernmost district of Bihar has also established itself as a Business hub of Bihar due to its well-connectivity with national capital New Delhi and Kolkata. Gaya is an upcoming Educational hub donning the two Central government funded institutions namely Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) and Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Bodhgaya beside a state government funded Magadh University.
By Train :
Gaya Junction (station code – GAYA) is an important station on Howrah – New Delhi route and connected to almost all parts of country with express and mail trains. Rajdhani Express trains plying between New Delhi – Howrah, New Delhi – Sealdah, New Delhi – Bhubaneswar, etc. have their stoppages at Gaya. Many passenger (local) trains ply between Gaya and Patna, Gaya and Deen Dayal Upadhyay Junction, Gaya and Barauni. The nearest major railway stations are Patna Junction (92 kms.), Barauni Junction (158 kms.), Deen Dayal Upadhyay Junction (232 kms.), Varanasi Junction (258 kms.), New Delhi (1050 kms.), Kolkata (460 kms.). Gaya Junction is a tourist and pilgrimage destination usually observe huge rush round the year, hence it is advised to book / reserve the tickets in advance.
By Road :
National Highway (NH) No. 19 between Delhi with Kolkata passes through Gaya and connects the city with major cities as well as other important destinations of India. National Highway (NH) No. 83 connects Gaya with Patna, the capital city of Bihar and north-eastern region of India. Buses run at frequent intervals between Patna and Gaya, it takes about 4 hours to travel between two destinations. From Patna buses are available for all the parts of Bihar.
By Air :
Gaya International Airport (IATA Code: GAY) is having domestic connectivity with Delhi, Kolkata, Mumbai, Varanasi, Bangaluru and other parts of India with limited flights operated by Air India and Indigo airline. Additionally, Gaya is directly connected to Bangkok, Yangon (Myanmar) and many cities of east Asian countries. Jay Prakash Narayan International Airport (Patna) is a major airport connected with several flights with Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Lucknow, Varanasi along with many other destinations. Distance of Patna Airport is about 100 kms. that can be reached by hiring a taxi.

pages.title: WORKSHOP ON NPS AND UPS FOR CUSB EMPLOYEES
pages.text:
WORKSHOP ON NPS AND UPS FOR CUSB EMPLOYEES
For the central Government employees, two pension schemes are currently available   viz., NPS and UPS. The National Pension System (NPS), launched by the Government of India and regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA), aims to build a pensioned society.  NPS has been mandatory for all Central Government employees joining service from 1st January 2004 onwards as part of their retirement benefits.  The Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) is a pension scheme introduced by the Government of India, effective 1st April 2025, as an option under the National Pension System (NPS) for Central Government employees. It is designed to provide assured, inflation-indexed, and adequate retirement benefits, addressing concerns of longevity protection and pension predictability. UPS operates within the existing NPS architecture regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) and is applicable to both serving and retired employees under specific conditions.
The Investment Strategy under Government NPS is such that the Funds were invested by default among 3 fund managers – SBI Pension, UTI Retirement solutions and LIC Pension.  Now, Central Government subscribers can select any Pension Fund Manager including Axis Pension Fund to manage his / her NPS investments.
In this background, it is a necessity that every employee should know the features of these pension schemes in order to invest their hard earned money for an assured and safe return.  Keeping this in mind, the AXIZ BANK has voluntarily come forward to conduct an awareness workshop on the features of NPS and UPS for the employees of CUSB.  The workshop is aimed for sensitising the different cohorts of employees like, newly joined employees, existing employees and those who are retiring within the next two to three years.
We, the Department of Commerce and Business Studies and Economic Studies and Policy cordially invite you all to be part of this workshop so as to understand the nitty-gritty of NPS and UPS for an informed decision on your investments in Pension Funds.  The details of the programme are here under:

pages.title: Deeksharambha - Orientation Programme for newly enrolled BBA LLB students at CUSB
pages.text:
Deeksharambha - Orientation Programme for newly enrolled BBA LLB students at CUSB
Legal education has made its foray into different areas including business domain as per the need of the market. The market-oriented courses like BBA LLB having a combination of business administration and law has a bright prospect and youths can make a promising career post completion of their studies. These statements were given by Dr. Vinita S. Sahay, Director, Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Bodhgaya during the "Deeksharambha: A Students Induction Programme organised for newly enrolled students BBA LLB programme at Central University of South Bihar (CUSB). As the chief guest Dr. Sahay emphasized upon the importance of legal education in today's world and further stated that legal education is now necessary in business and commerce also. She also shared some handy tips with students who have enrolled in the newly launched Five-Year Integrated BBA LLB programme from the session 2024-29.
In the presidential address CUSB Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh lauded the efforts of the department of Law for fulfilling the essential criteria as per Bar Council India (BCI) to get recognition for BBA LLB programme. The course has received overwhelming response from the candidates belonging to different states of India that is quite encouraging for us. We have established ourselves as an institution of academic excellence and with the inclusion of such market-oriented courses we would be able to find a respectable place for the University in the global rankings
Earlier the orientation programme organised by the SLG in collaboration with the Department of Commerce and Business Studies was formally inaugurated by VC Prof. K. N. Singh along with the chief guest IIM-BG Director Dr. Vinita S. Sahay, Prof. Sanjay Prakash Srivastava, Dean & Head, School of Law and Governance (SLG), Prof. Brajesh Kumar, Head, Commerce, Prof. Subramanian Shanmugam, Dean, Management, Programme Co-ordinator Prof. Pradip Kumar Das, faculty members of SLG and other departments.
Prof. S. P. Srivastava in his welcome speech welcomed the new students and highlighted the unique blend of business and legal skills that the students would acquire, preparing them for successful careers in a rapidly evolving world, legal and business world. Further, Prof. Brajesh Kumar, Head, Commerce shared valuable insights and advice with the students, encouraging them to embrace the challenges and opportunities that will lie ahead. Prof. S. Shanmugam, Dean of commerce and business studies, highlighted the importance of law in business nowadays contributing to societal progress. The students, who were visibly excited and motivated by the addresses of the dignitaries and expressed their gratitude for the opportunity to learn from such an accomplished individual. They acknowledged the immense responsibility that comes with pursuing a legal career and pledged to strive for excellence in their studies.
The Deeksharambha ceremony was a memorable occasion that marked the beginning of a promising journey for the first batch of BBA LL.B. students. The ceremony concluded with a vote of thanks delivered by the Prof. Pradip Kumar Das and shared the university's commitment to providing a conducive learning environment and equipping the students with the necessary skills to succeed in their chosen field.

pages.title: Eminent Scientist Prof. Shekhar C. Mande delivers lecture on India’s Journey in Science Through Centuries at CUSB
pages.text:
Eminent Scientist Prof. Shekhar C. Mande delivers lecture on India’s Journey in Science Through Centuries at CUSB
The Research and Development Cell (RDC) of Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) along with the departments of Biotechnology and Life Science organized a guest lecture on ‘India’s Journey in Science Through Centuries’. The lecture organised to let students know about the contribution of India in Science in Vedic as well as modern time was attended by over 350 students and 50 faculty members at Vivekanand Auditorium of CUSB. The special lecture was delivered by an Eminent, Iconic & Decorated Scientist of Present time, Prof. Shekhar C. Mande, a renowned Structural Biologist of India and Shanti Shwaroop Bhatnagar awardee, Former-Director General, Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), Secretary, Secretary of the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology and President, Vijnana Bharati.
Prof. Mande introduced a narrative of colonial power that Indians had no idea about science. But the fact is that the Indian contribution in science was either masked or suppressed. He provided facts about the ancient contribution of Indians in science such as discovery of Zero (0), lost-wax process, surgery and plastic surgery, metallurgy and so on. He also talked about the ancient dentistry practices for which archaeological evidences are collected from Mohenjo-Daro and the findings have been published in Nature. He also highlighted the role of Acharya Praful Chandra Ray in developing Rashayan Sastra in India. He also stresses upon the holistic approach that ancient Indians have practiced about Panchmahabootas. He also talked about the contribution of Indian scientists especially in developing technology for milk powder making from buffalo milk, vaccines and several other local technologies. He emphasized that we need to focus on developing local techniques, and work for the nation with empathy and patriotism to make India Developed by 2047 for which we have a clear-cut vision ahead. Prof. Mande also introduced students to Vijnana Bharati, a largest volunteer based organizing working to popularize Swadeshi science in India and across the world.
As the Patron CUSB Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh emphasized upon the need for such talks that would fulfil the mandate required to fulfil one of the important requirements about NEP 2020. The talk highlights the need of the Indian Knowledge System (IKS) to be included in each course. Prof. Singh also talked about an incident of Epic Ramayana in which when lord Rama decided to dry the ocean, the lord of Ocean requested him not to do as it is a natural resource needed to make balance on mother earth, which tells us about the balance of resources on the ecosystem.
CUSB Public Relation Officer (PRO) Mohammad Mudassir Alam said that earlier the convenor of the program, Prof. Durg Vijai Singh, Director RDC delivered a welcome address. The co- convenor Prof. Rakesh Kumar, Head Biotechnology and Prof. Ram Pratap Singh, Head Life Science informed about the lecture series and introduced the guest to the audience. Secretary, Dr. Prabhat Ranjan (Head Computer Science Department) delivered a vote of thanks. Deans, Heads, and Faculty members of a large number of departments actively along with Prof. R. K Singh, OSD, Rashmi Tripathi (Finance Officer), attended the talk.

pages.title: Swachhta Hi Seva Pakhwada, September 17-October 02, 2024
pages.text:
Swachhta Hi Seva Pakhwada, September 17-October 02, 2024
Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) is fully committed to adopt the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and fundamental principles laid down for educational institutions as well as the individual institutions studying and working in them. NEP 2020 gives prominence to ethics and human values such as cleanliness, spirit of service, respect for public property, personal and public hygiene, teamwork and cooperation etc. CUSB has fully adopted NEP 2020 in its curriculum and daily activities and in its context the university is committed to personal and public hygiene. These statements were made by Vice Chancellor of Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh at the inaugural ceremony of ‘Swachhata Hi Seva Pakhwada 2024’. The Vice Chancellor formally started the fortnight by pronouncing the slogan 'Savabhaav Swachhata, Sanskar Sanskar Swachhata' at the main gate of the university. Addressing the students, professors, officers and staff of CUSB, Vice Chancellor Prof. Singh said that everyone will take care of their personal hygiene as well as the cleanliness of the university campus, their homes and the surrounding areas. He appealed to the people present at the venue to do 'voluntary cleanliness work' on October 1 at the last stage of the fortnight and realize the dream of Father of the Nation Mahatma Gandhi of complete cleanliness.
After his address, the Vice Chancellor started the 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2024' campaign by sweeping the main gate of the University, which will run till October 2, the birth anniversary of Father of the Nation Mahatma Gandhi. Taking inspiration from the values of public cleanliness in NEP 2020, Vice Chancellor Prof Singh himself cleaned the public bus stand near the main gate of the university by sweeping it, so that commuters can sit comfortably. Under the 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2024' campaign, under the 'Campus for Community' resolution of the Vice Chancellor, the sides of National Highway No. 120 from the main gate to Dharamshala and Panchanpur have been cleaned.
Vice Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh was accompanied by Registrar Prof. Narendra Kumar Rana, Finance Officer Mrs. Rashmi Tripathi, Controller of Examinations Dr. Shantigopal Pain, DSW Prof. Pawan Kumar Mishra, Proctor Prof. Pranav Kumar, NSS Program Coordinator Dr. Budhendra Kumar Singh, NCC ANO Lieutenant (Dr) Pragya Gupta, Librarian Dr. Pramod Kumar Singh, Deputy Registrar Pratish Kumar Das, Assistant Registrar Shashi Ranjan, etc. Along with the university administrative department, students who are members of the National Service Scheme (NSS) unit, students who are members of the National Cadet Corps (NCC) unit, Dean Students Welfare (DSW) office, Deans and Heads of various departments, hostel wardens, supporting outsourcing staff played an important role in making the program successful. It is known that under the 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2024' fortnight, many programs based on cleanliness will be organized in the CUSB campus and surrounding areas for the next 15 days.

pages.title: Awareness campaign cum tree plantation program by CUSB's Agriculture Department
pages.text:
Awareness campaign cum tree plantation program by CUSB's Agriculture Department
Under the 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign launched by Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi keeping in mind environmental protection and its responsibilities, an awareness campaign cum tree plantation program was organized by the Agriculture Department of Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) on 17th September, 2024. In the tree plantation program organized in the agricultural field of the university, Vice Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh along with Registrar Prof. Narendra Kumar Rana planted a tree in the name of mother. DSW Prof. Pawan Kumar Mishra, Prof. Rati Kant Kumbhar, Dr. Manglesh Kumar Mangalam, Prof. Vivek Dave, Dr. Abod Kumar, Librarian Dr. Pramod Kumar Singh, Mrs. Renu, Dr. Rachna Vishwakarma, Assistant Registrar Shashi Ranjan, professors of Agriculture Faculty and students and staff were present in the tree plantation program. Vice Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh appealed to the people present in the program that all of you should take a pledge today that you must plant a tree in the name of mother to protect the earth, only then the goal of water, life and greenery can be achieved.
Before the tree plantation program, an awareness campaign program (seminar) was organized by the Department of Agriculture under the guidance of the Vice Chancellor. The program was conducted by Dr. Hemant Kumar Singh (Assistant Professor) in which the faculty members and students of the Faculty of Agriculture presented their views on the topic 'One tree in the name of mother' through Hindi-English speeches, poems, essays and sher-wa-shayari etc. On this occasion, awareness programs were presented on the impact of environment and climate on environmental conservation and biodiversity and global impacts. In the program, the Head of Department and Dean of the Faculty of Agriculture, Prof. Ram Ashish Yadav presented a lecture on the utility and need of a tree. Among the faculty members of agriculture, Prof. Prabhat Kumar Singh, Dr. Pranav Tripathi and others also presented awareness lectures. The responsibilities of technical support in the program were discharged by Manoj Kumar Singh, Laboratory Assistant of Faculty of Agriculture.

'Anvay Aarambh' orientation program was organized for the new students of Gargi Sadan Girls Hostel of Central University of South Bihar (CUSB). The orientation program was organized under the patronage of Vice Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh by Chief Warden Mrs. Renu with the help of Warden Dr. Neha Shukla, students and other staff. Registrar Prof. Narendra Singh Rana, DSW Prof. Pawan Kumar Mishra, Proctor Prof. Pranav Kumar, Nodal Officer of Anti-Ragging Dr. Javed Ahsan etc. were present as chief guests in the program organized in Vivekananda Lecture Complex under the chairmanship of Vice Chancellor.
In his presidential address, Vice Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh said that the importance of girls has been equal in our society and without them the society cannot develop in a better way. My wish and thinking is that by studying here, our girls should earn a name in the country and the world. The more they go ahead, the more the glory of this university will increase. The Vice Chancellor said that the university administration is constantly working for the convenience of the girl students and is ready to provide better facilities in future as well. Emphasizing on cooperation and mutual coordination among the girl students, he said that many things get solved automatically by living with a team spirit.
Earlier the program organized for the new girl students started with lighting of lamps and Kulgeet. Thereafter, Chief Warden of Gargi Sadan Girls Hostel, Mrs. Renu, while welcoming all the guests, mentioned the residential facilities available for the girl students in the university and the hostel and also presented the outline of the upcoming action plan.
On this occasion, Dean of Student Welfare (DSW) Prof. Pawan Kumar Mishra explained in detail the facilities provided to the girl students. Proctor Prof. Pranav Kumar stressed on safety and discipline within the university campus. Dr. Javed Ahsan, Nodal Officer of Anti Ragging, while creating awareness about ragging, said that this campus is free from ragging. We all can stay away from ragging by being alert and aware of it. The mentoring system and the counselling process available for it were also explained in detail.
On this occasion, Hostel Coordinator Prof. Kiran Kumari, Deputy Registrar Pratish Das, Head of Anti Ragging Squad Prof. Ratikant Kumbhakar, Head of Media Department Prof. Shiv Shankar, Head of Psychology Department Prof. Vijay Mishra, Head of Agricultural Science Prof. Ramashish Yadav, Deputy Chief Proctor Prof. Manglesh Mangalam, Assistant Proctor Dr. Abodh Kumar, Dr. Sujit Kumar, Dr. Bibash Mohapatra, Dr. Rachna Vishwakarma, Dr. Moni Roy, Dr. Poonam Kumari, Dr. Vikal Singh, Warden of Boys Hostel Dr. Manjit Singh, Dr. Kishore Kumar were present.
The program was organized by Warden of Gargi House Dr. Neha Shukla along with Vedika, Tanu Deepanjali, Geetanjali, Simran, Suruchi, Sakshi, Fauzia, Shravya, Hema Khanni as volunteers. The program was conducted by student Aastha Bharti and the vote of thanks was given by Warden Dr. Pratishtha Sonkar.

pages.title: Blood Donation Camp by National Service Scheme Unit of CUSB, 13th September, 2024
pages.text:
Blood Donation Camp by National Service Scheme Unit of CUSB, 13th September, 2024
In order to discharge social responsibilities, the National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) organized a voluntary blood donation camp in collaboration with Anugrah Narayan Medical College and Hospital (ANMCH), Gaya. Under the patronage of Vice Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh, the camp was organized by Dr. Budhendra Kumar Singh, NSS Program Coordinator, CUSB, with the help of Dr. Priya Ranjan (NSS Program Officer), NSS volunteers and students of other departments.
A total 55 people donated blood in the voluntary blood donation camp organized at the School of Education (Malviya Bhawan) of the University. Dr. Budhendra Kumar Singh appreciated the volunteers of the NSS unit for coordinating the blood donation camp, providing refreshments to the blood donors and creating awareness about the importance of regular blood donation.
Program Coordinator Dr. Budhendra Kumar Singh said that in line with the broad objectives of NSS, this initiative reflects the university's commitment towards social responsibilities and encourages the youth to contribute to the welfare of the society. With this objective, this philanthropic event organized in the university campus saw active participation of students, faculty members and volunteers who donated blood voluntarily. He informed that a dedicated medical team from ANMCH, Gaya was present at the camp to conduct the blood donation process smoothly and safely. The camp was supported wholeheartedly by the Magadh Medical technical staff.

pages.title: A Brainstorming session and meeting of External AI Experts with members of Board of Studies
pages.text:
A Brainstorming session and meeting of External AI Experts with members of Board of Studies
Brainstorming session, 28th & 29th, April 2023
The Department of Computer Science at the Central University of South Bihar held a brainstorming session and meeting with external AI experts on April 28th and 29th, 2023, to discuss the M.Sc. in Artificial Intelligence program’s course structure as per NEP-2020. The programme was done under the guidance and leadership of the Honourable Vice Chancellor. The session was led by Dr. Prabhat Ranjan, the Head of the Department.
External experts included prominent professors from JNU, NIT Kurukshetra, NIT Patna, IIT Patna, and the Central University of Jharkhand. Internal members from the Computer Science Department and the Department of Mathematics also participated.
During the session, experts interacted with students, discussing the significance of AI, machine learning, and the potential of AI to revolutionize various fields. The experts provided real-life examples and addressed misconceptions about AI.
The Board of Studies (BOS) meeting concluded with recommendations for new courses such as Human-Computer Interaction, Time Series Analysis & Forecasting, Cyber Security, Data Visualization, Python Programming & AI Lab, Mathematical Foundation for AI, and Big Data. Non-credit courses in IPR, Innovation and Entrepreneurship, and Soft Skills were also suggested.
As a result, the Department drafted a new course framework for the M.Sc. in Artificial Intelligence based on these recommendations.

pages.title: Webinar on Regulatory Affairs by Dept. of Pharmacy, May 05, 2026
pages.text:
Webinar on Regulatory Affairs by Dept. of Pharmacy, May 05, 2026
A webinar on Navigating Regulatory Affairs: Trends, Practices and Industry Insights was successfully organised by the Department of Pharmacy under the School of Health Science, Central University of South Bihar, in association with the Pharmakon Club. Prof. D. Sreedhar from Manipal College of Pharmaceutical Sciences, MAHE delivered the expert talk. He elaborated on the current landscape of pharmaceutical regulatory affairs and emerging career opportunities. The speaker highlighted recent industry trends, compliance requirements, and the importance of regulatory strategies in drug development and approval processes. The lecture also guided participants on career opportunities and the skills needed to excel in regulatory affairs.
The program was conducted under the patronage of the Hon’ble Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh. The Chairperson of the event, Prof. Subrat Kumar Bhattamisra, Dean, School of Health Science, has delivered the welcome address and the webinar was convened by Prof. Vivek Dave, Head of the Department of Pharmacy. The vote of thanks was delivered by the organising secretary, Dr Arun Kumar, while Dr Gireesh Kumar Singh and Dr Bibhash Chandra Mohanta served as members of the organising committee. The webinar witnessed enthusiastic participation of more than 100 students, research scholars, and faculty members, making it an engaging and impactful academic interaction. Participants also appreciated the relevance of the topic and the expert insights shared during the session. Participants expressed that such academic initiatives play an important role in bridging the gap between academia and industry while enhancing the professional competencies of students.

pages.title: Community feast, 'Krishi Shramyogi – Samrasata Sahabhoj' on the occasion of the Autumn Harvest at CUSB, April 06, 2026
pages.text:
Community feast, 'Krishi Shramyogi – Samrasata Sahabhoj' on the occasion of the Autumn Harvest at CUSB, April 06, 2026
In one of its kind unique initiatives, the Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) organised 'Krishi Shramyogi – Samrasata Sahabhoj' (Agricultural Laborer – Harmony Community Feast) on the Occasion of the Autumn Harvest. On this occasion, CUSB Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh said that respect for labor within society is an indispensable prerequisite for achieving the goals of a 'Self-Reliant India' (Atmanirbhar Bharat) and a 'Developed India' (Viksit Bharat). It is noteworthy that the Harmony Feast was organized by the faculty members of the Department of Agriculture for the laborers engaged in agricultural work, as a gesture of respect for their efforts. Prof. Singh observed that, currently, there is a growing tendency to view manual labor through a negative lens, and the youth are increasingly becoming averse to physical work, a trend that poses a matter of concern for the future of agriculture. The fundamental spirit and objective behind this 'Harmony Community Feast' is to restore dignity to labor and to foster a sense of equality and affectionate care towards the laborers.
Distinguished guests participating in the 'Harmony Community Feast' included Mahant Shri Pratyānand Ji and Shri Vivekananda Ji from the Shri Shankaracharya Math, Bodh Gaya, as well as Dr. Indresh Kumar, Guide (Convener) of the Muslim Rashtriya Manch (MRM). Other attendees at the event included CUSB Registrar Prof. Narendra Kumar Rana, Finance Officer Smt. Rashmi Tripathi, Controller of Examinations Dr. Shantigopal Pine, Deputy Proctor Dr. Manglesh Kumar Mangalam, Anti-Ragging Nodal Officer Dr. Javed Ahsan, Deputy Registrars Shri Pratish Kumar Das and Shri Kumar Kaushal, Chief Warden Smt. Renu, Head of the School of Agriculture Prof. Avanish Prakash Singh, Dr. Hemant Kumar Sing, Prof. Ram Ashish Yadav were accompanied by other faculty members and students from the department. In the community feast organized to mark the harvest of the Sharad (autumn) crops, Vice-Chancellor Prof. K.N. Singh honored the agricultural laborers by presenting them with ‘gamchas’ and sarees as gifts. Participating in the community feast, the laborers expressed their delight and conveyed their gratitude.

समाज में श्रम के प्रति सम्मान, आत्मनिर्भर भारत एवं विकसित भारत के लक्ष्य की प्राप्ति के लिए अपरिहार्य आवश्यक है | उक्त वक्तव्य दक्षिण बिहार केन्द्रीय विश्वविद्यालय (सीयूएसबी), गया के कुलपति प्रो. कामेश्वर नाथ सिंह ने कृषि एवं विकास संकाय द्वारा आयोजित 'कृषि श्रमयोगी समरसता सहभोज' के अवसर पर दिया | ज्ञातव्य है कि वासंतिक फसलों की प्रक्रियात्मक पूर्बल के अवसर पर  सीयूएसबी परिसर में कृषि कार्य में लगे श्र्मयोगियों के सम्मान में श्रमिकों के साथ कृषि संकाय के शिक्षकों द्वारा समरसता भोज का आयोजन परिसर में किया गया | प्रो. सिंह ने कहा कि आज श्रम को नकारात्मक दृष्टि से देखने की प्रकृति को बढ़ावा मिल रहा है एवं युवा वर्ग भी श्रम से विमुख होता जा रहा है, जो कृषि के भविष्य के लिए चिंता का विषय है | श्रम को प्रतिष्ठित करने एवं श्रमिकों को समता एवं मंमता का भाव जागृत करना ही समरसता सहभोज की भाव - भावना है |
समरसता सहभोज में सम्मानित अतिथि के रूप पर श्री शंकराचार्य मठ, बोधगया के महंत श्री प्रत्यानन्द जी एवं श्री विवेकानंद जी तथा मुस्लिम राष्ट्रीय मंच (एमआरएम) के मार्गदर्शक (संयोजक) डॉ. इंद्रेश कुमार शामिल हुए | इस कार्यक्रम में सीयूएसबी के कुलसचिव प्रो नरेंद्र कुमार राणा, वित्ताधिकारी श्रीमती रश्मि त्रिपाठी, परीक्षा नियंत्रक डॉ. शांतिगोपाल पाइन, डिप्टी प्रॉक्टर डॉ. मंगलेश कुमार मंगलम, एंटी रैगिंग नोडल ऑफिसर डॉ. जावेद अहसन,  उपकुलसचिव श्री प्रतीश कुमार दास, उपकुलसचिव श्री कुमार कौशल, चीफ वार्डन श्रीमती रेनू, कृषि संकाय के अध्यक्ष प्रो अवनिश प्रकाश, डॉ. हेमंत कुमार, प्रो. राम आशीष यादव के साथ विभाग के अन्य शिक्षक एवं छात्र - छात्राएं मौजूद थे | शारदीय फसलोत्पादन के अवसर पर आयोजित कृषि श्रमयोगी - समरसता सहभोज के अवसर पर कुलपति प्रो के. एन. सिंह ने श्रमयोगियों को गमछा एवं साड़ी उपहारस्वरूप देकर सम्मानित किया | कुलपति महोदय के संरक्षण में आयोजित सहभोज में शामिल होकर श्रमयोगियों ने प्रसन्नता व्यक्त करते हुए आभार प्रकट किया |

pages.title: AVINYA 3.0 Cross continental conference organised by the SLG & IIC of CUSB, April 26, 2026
pages.text:
AVINYA 3.0 Cross continental conference organised by the SLG & IIC of CUSB, April 26, 2026
AVINYA 3.0 Cross continental conference ; organised by School of Law and Governance in collaboration with Institution Innovation Council, Department of Physical Education, and NIPAM.
The School of Law and Governance in collaboration with The Institutions Innovation Council (IIC), the Department of Physical Education, and the National Intellectual Property Awareness Mission (NIPAM), inaugurated AVINYA 3.0. This cross-continental conference revolved around the theme IP and Sports: Ready, Set, Innovate! to examine how intellectual property (IP) underpins the global sports industry. Held under the patronage of Honble Vice Chancellor Prof. (Dr.) K. N. Singh, the event brought together international experts to explore the connections between law, technology, and athletic performance. The session opened with leadership addresses that set a strategic tone for the day. Prof. Dr. Venktesh Singh, President of IIC at CUSB, emphasized that a developed economy requires strong IP consciousness in sports. Building on this, Prof. Dr. Ashok Kumar, Dean of the School of Law and Governance, presented the concept note and underlined the urgent need for structured engagement with sports law across Asia. Prof. Usha Tiwari, Head of the Department of Physical Education and a key organizer, highlighted the necessity of interdisciplinary collaboration between physical education and legal frameworks to safeguard sporting innovation.
As discussions progressed, speakers explored sports as complex commercial ecosystems. Prof. Sameek Sen (WBNUJS) contrasted Indias reactive IP framework with proactive, event-specific legislation used globally to prevent ambush marketing. From a technological perspective, Prof. Hayri Ertan (Turkey) shared biomechanical research on Olympic archers , while Prof. Subhrajit Chanda (Jindal Global Law School) raised questions regarding the ownership of AI-generated data and athlete digital twins . Adding an economic dimension, Dr. Gururaj Devarhubli and Dr. Chandrakant Dheeman noted that IP acts as the invisible engine driving billions in revenue through broadcasting rights, equipment patents like the Nike Vaporfly, and merchandising.
The conference also addressed pressing challenges and mapped out a future direction. Chief Guest Prof. (Dr.) Pushpinder Singh Gill, vice chancellor, Maharaj Bhupinder Singh Sports University, Punjab emphasized the importance of swift legal remedies, such as John Doe orders, to tackle illegal streaming and piracy in real time. He further advocated for simpler, affordable IP systems to support grassroots innovators. Guest of Honor Dr. Indu Mazumdar, Dean, School of Physical Education, ITM University Gwalior added a vital perspective, explaining how athletes today are not just competitors but brands in their own right, with image rights extending even to personal elements like signature celebrations and tattoos. She reinforced the economic dimension of the sector, noting how IP protection sustains the business of sports through broadcasting and licensing. The event concluded with a strong call for a unified national framework for sports-related IP in India. In the closing vote of thanks by Dr. Sunaina, participants recognized that the future of sports depends on how effectively intellectual property is managed and protected.

pages.title: Blood Donation Camp organized by NSS Unit of CUSB, April 24, 2026
pages.text:
Blood Donation Camp organized by NSS Unit of CUSB, April 24, 2026
A blood donation camp was organized by the National Service Scheme (NSS) unit of the Central University of South Bihar (CUSB), in joint collaboration with Anugrah Memorial College, Gayaji. Held under the patronage of Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh at the Yoga Center Hall within Malviya Bhawan, the camp saw members of the CUSB family voluntarily donate blood. Vice-Chancellor Prof. K.N. Singh lauded the blood donation camp organized by the NSS, describing it as an act of true service and social work. Despite the sudden rise in temperatures over the past few days and the commencement of semester examinations in the coming days, students demonstrated great enthusiasm for blood donation, resulting in the collection of a total of 42 units of blood.
The blood donation camp was organized and led by NSS Program Officer Dr. Parijat Pradhan, under the guidance of NSS Coordinator Prof. Usha Tiwari. Speaking on the occasion, Prof. Tiwari described blood donation as a crucial aspect of nation-building and social service. The Dean of Student Welfare, Prof. Pawan Kumar Mishra, also encouraged the CUSB students and emphasized the significance of viewing the objective of the blood donation camp through the lens of the campus community network. Prominent among the faculty members from various faculties and departments who participated in the event were Prof. M. Vijay Kumar Sharma, Dr. Haresh Narayan Pandey, Dr. Priya Ranjan, Dr. Rinki, Dr. Anil Kumar, Dr. Rohit Kumar, Dr. Anand Gupta, among others. Students from various departments of the university—including Ritik Kumar Singh, Bharat Prasad, Ritik, Madhusudan, Shivam, Saurav, Vedika, Prerana, Nandini, Kajal, Abhishek, Prem Prakash, Anurag, Shikha, and others—also contributed to the program by serving as volunteers.

pages.title: Webinar on Food, Planet & Earth by NSS Unit of CUSB, April 23, 2026
pages.text:
Webinar on Food, Planet & Earth by NSS Unit of CUSB, April 23, 2026
A webinar on the theme Food | Planet | Earth was successfully conducted on 23rd April 2026 at the Seminar Hall, Room No. 206, Department of Physical Education, School of Education, Central University of South Bihar. The event was organized under the aegis of the National Service Scheme (NSS). The program was conducted under the guidance and supervision of Prof. Usha Tiwari, NSS Coordinator, and Dr. Rahul Singh, Assistant Professor of Physical Education and Program Coordinator.
The keynote speaker for the session was Nirja Dhillon, representing Vegan Outreach. She delivered an insightful and engaging session on veganism, focusing on the relationship between food systems, environmental sustainability, and ethical treatment of animals. During the webinar, the speaker highlighted the rapid growth of the food industry and raised awareness about the ethical concerns associated with animal-based products. She explained how animals are often subjected to unnatural conditions, including forced production beyond their natural capacity, use of chemical injections, and artificial methods to increase milk and meat production. The session encouraged participants to reflect on sustainable and cruelty-free food choices.
The webinar was highly interactive, with students actively participating in the question- and-answer session, where they raised thoughtful queries and engaged in meaningful discussion with the speaker. The program concluded with a vote of thanks delivered by Anant Sandilya, Research Scholar, Department of Physical Education, who expressed gratitude to the speaker, organizers, and participants for making the event a success. Overall, the webinar proved to be highly informative and thought-provoking, leaving participants with greater awareness about veganism, sustainability, and ethical food practices.

pages.title: Tree Plantation on the occasion of World Earth Day at CUSB, April 22, 2026
pages.text:
Tree Plantation on the occasion of World Earth Day at CUSB, April 22, 2026
To mark the observance of World Earth Day, the Department of Geology at CUSB organized a tree plantation drive within the university campus. Led by Vice-Chancellor Prof. K. N. Singh, the morning of World Earth Day commenced with a tree plantation activity within the residential complex premises of CUSB. Dedicated to environmental conservation, the event witnessed enthusiastic participation from faculty members, officials, staff, and students from various departments. In his address, Prof. K. N. Singh appealed to everyone present at the venue to promote energy conservation and utilize renewable resources in order to save the earth. He emphasized that we must plant as many trees as possible to ensure the safety and preservation of our environment an
d our planet. Furthermore, he urged that alongside planting trees, we should each adopt at least one tree and take full responsibility for its care, including watering and providing fertilizer. On the occasion of Earth Day, the Dept. of Geology also organized a painting competition in which participating students beautifully showcased their creativity. Prof. Prafull Kumar Singh, Head, Geology mentioned that the winner of the poster-making competition held on the theme 'Our Power, Our Planet' would receive a cash prize of ₹3,000. The participant securing the second position will receive ₹2,000, while the third-place winner will be awarded ₹1,000. Dr. Milankumar Sharma, Dr. Vikal Kumar Singh, Dr. Dhirendra Kumar, and other faculty members of the department played a pivotal role in organizing this event.

pages.title: Dept. of Physics organizes lecture on Photonic Chips, Quantum Computing, April 17, 2026
pages.text:
Dept. of Physics organizes lecture on Photonic Chips, Quantum Computing, April 17, 2026
The Department of Physics at the Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) organized a special lecture on the topic, "Photonic Chips for Neutral Atom Quantum Computing." Mr. Sanjeet Kumar, a researcher with the Neuromorphic Quantum Photonics Group at the Kirchhoff Institute of Physics, Heidelberg University (Germany), served as the keynote speaker at this event. During his lecture, Mr. Sanjeet Kumar explained how powerful quantum computers can be developed by utilizing light (photonics) and neutral atoms. He discussed in detail the fabrication of photonic chips, the challenges associated with them, and their practical applications. Furthermore, he shared insights into his current research work, which involves the development of an electro-optic phase modulator designed to control atoms using UV light. Addressing the students during the session, he emphasized that in today's world, acquiring practical skills—rather than merely theoretical knowledge—is of paramount importance to enable students to advance in their careers. The event organized under the patronage of Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameshwara Nath Singh, was attended by senior faculty member Prof. Venkatesh Singh, along with other faculty members of the department and students. Following the formal inauguration of the program, research scholar Rajiv welcomed the guests, while Dr. Lakhwinder Singh, Assistant Professor, delivered the vote of thanks at the conclusion of the event. During the lecture, students posed pertinent questions related to the subject matter and gained valuable new insights.

pages.title: Felicitation of Bharat BoudhIKS National Examination 2026 toppers at NIT Patna, April 19, 2026
pages.text:
Felicitation of Bharat BoudhIKS National Examination 2026 toppers at NIT Patna, April 19, 2026
Students of Central University of South Bihar, Gaya given outstanding performance at the State Level in the All India Bharat BoudhIKS National Examination 2026 Based on Indian Knowledge Tradition, Organized by Vidya Bharati Uchcha Shiksha Sansthan Under the able leadership and guidance of the Honble Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh, the Central University of South Bihar (CUSB), Gaya successfully participated in the All India Bharat BoudhIKS National Examination (BBIKSNE) 2026, based on Indian Knowledge Tradition, organized by Vidya Bharati Uccha Shiksha Sansthan on 31 January 2026. The students of CUSB delivered an outstanding performance at the South Bihar provincial level.
Prof. Singh remarked that the nature of this examination not only strengthens subject understanding but also helps in preparing for upcoming competitive examinations. It further enables youth to deeply understand and imbibe Indian culture and values, while promoting the integration of Indian knowledge traditions into higher education. He described this initiative as a strong and commendable effort of Vidya Bharati Uchcha Shiksha Sansthan towards achieving the goals of the National Education Policy 2020 (NEP).
The Examination Coordinator, Dr. Tarun Kumar Tyagi (Department of Teacher Education) and Member Secretary (VBUSS, Dakshin Bihar Prant), informed that a total of 10 students from CUSB achieved excellent positions at Bihar Prant level in the BBIKSNE 2026:
•    1st Position: Anshu Kumar (Department of Historical Studies & Archaeology)
•    2nd Position: Shruti Mishra (Department of Agriculture)
•    3rd & 4th Positions: Shubhangi Singh and Beauty Kumari (Department of Teacher Education)
•    5th Position: Abhishek Kumar (Department of Library and Information Science)
•    6th Position: Anshu Priya (Department of Physics)
•    7th Position: Shubham Kumar (Department of Biotechnology)
•    8th & 9th Positions: Premlata and Jatin Kumar (Department of Teacher Education)
•    10th Position: Pragati Priya (Department of Psychological Science)
These students were honored for their outstanding performance in a one-day Regional Seminar and Felicitation Ceremony for Rank Holders of Bharat BoudhIKS National Examination 2026, organized by the National Institute of Technology (NIT), Patna. The ceremony was graced by the presence of Shri K. N. Raghunandan Jee, National Organization Secretary, Vidya Bharati Uchcha Shiksha Sanstha; Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh, Vice-Chancellor, CUSB Gaya; Prof. Pradeep Kumar Jain, Director, NIT Patna; and Prof. Raman Kumar Trivedi, Regional Coordinator, VBUSS (Bihar and Jharkhand).
On this occasion, all students were awarded with their Rank Certificates. Additionally, four students received a cash prize of ₹2500 each, while six students were given consolation prizes of ₹500 each.
The event was also graced by the esteemed presence of Controller of Examinations of CUSB, Dr. Shantigopal Paine; Deputy Registrar, Shri Kumar Kaushal; Dean of Student Welfare, Prof. Pawan Kumar Mishra; Members of the advisory committee (BBIKSNE, CUSB); Heads of Departments; Deans of Schools; and more than 50 faculty members from CUSB who encouraged and motivated the students for their excellent performance.
On this auspicious occasion, the Hon’ble Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh, Registrar, Prof. Narendra Kumar Rana, and Regional Coordinator of Vidya Bharati Higher Education Institute, Prof. Raman Kumar Trivedi, expressed their gratitude to the Bharat BoudIKS Examination Team (Centre, State & CUSB), advisory committee members, faculty, staff, office personnel, and VBUSS (Dakshin Bihar Prant) members for their contributions. They also motivated students to actively participate in future academic activities and strive for greater achievements.

pages.title: Special lecture on the 135th Birth Anniversary of Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar, April 13, 2026
pages.text:
Special lecture on the 135th Birth Anniversary of Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar, April 13, 2026
A special lecture was organized by the Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe (SC/ST) Cell of the Central University of South Bihar (CUSB), in collaboration with the Department of Law and Governance, on the occasion of the 135th birth anniversary of Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar. Held under the guidance of Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameswar Nath Singh, the program—themed "Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's Contribution to Social Justice and the Indian Constitution"—featured Prof. Rajesh Paswan from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi, as the keynote speaker. On this occasion, the book *Hindi Kavita Mein Baba Saheb Ambedkar* (Baba Saheb Ambedkar in Hindi Poetry)—authored by Dr. Kamalanand Arya—was jointly released by Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameswar Nath Singh, keynote speaker Prof. Rajesh Paswan, and Prof. Ashok Kumar.
In his address, keynote speaker Prof. Rajesh Paswan of JNU, New Delhi, presented an in-depth analysis of Dr. Ambedkar's life struggles, intellectual contributions, and constitutional vision. He stated that Dr. Ambedkar did not merely draft the Constitution; rather, he envisioned a society founded upon the principles of equality, liberty, and fraternity. Addressing the students, he remarked that the path to success lies through discipline, continuous study, and logical reasoning. Emphasizing women's empowerment as a crucial foundation for social progress, Prof. Paswan asserted that the establishment of a true democracy remains impossible until all sections of society—particularly women and marginalized communities—are empowered. He urged the youth to imbibe Dr. Ambedkar's ideas, scientific temper, commitment to constitutional values, and sense of social responsibility in their own lives, noting that only then could the construction of a strong and just nation be realized.
In his presidential address, Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameswar Nath Singh highlighted Dr. Ambedkar's "Nation First" approach, describing him as a source of inspiration for generations past, present, and future. Citing the thoughts of Martin Luther King Jr., he further shed light on the universal significance of equality and justice. Public Relations Officer (PRO) Mohammad Mudassir Alam stated that, following the formal inauguration of the program, Dr. Chandana Subba extended a warm welcome to the guests, speakers, and participants, observing that Dr. Ambedkar's life stands as a symbol of struggle, education, and an unwavering commitment to social justice. In his address, Prof. Ashok Kumar, Head of the Department of Law and Governance, emphasized the significance of social equality, equal opportunity, and the prohibition of discrimination, citing Articles 14, 15, 16, and 17 of the Indian Constitution. As part of the event, a collective reading of the Preamble to the Constitution and an oath-taking ceremony were also conducted.
The occasion was graced by the distinguished presence of Prof. Sanjay Prakash Srivastava, Prof. Pradeep Kumar Das, Dr. Dev Narayan, Dr. Anurag Agarwal, Dr. Poonam Kumari, Dr. Chandana Subba, Dr. Sunaina, and Dr. Niharika Singh, alongside Mr. Balam Rajak and Mr. Albinus Topno—members of the Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe Cell. The program concluded with a vote of thanks delivered by Dr. Sunaina.

pages.title: Special Discussion Session on ‘Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023’ Held at CUSB – April 10, 2026
pages.text:
Special Discussion Session on ‘Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023’ Held at CUSB – April 10, 2026
Under the joint aegis of the School of Social Sciences and Policy and its various constituent departments at the Central University of South Bihar (CUSB), a significant special discussion session was organized on the topic: "Immediate Implementation of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023: Issues and Imperatives." This event proved to be a robust platform for serious deliberation on contemporary issues related to women's empowerment and political participation. The program was presided over by the University's Honorable Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh. In his presidential address, he stated that the 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023'—introduced by the Government of India—is, in reality, a historic initiative aimed at honoring and empowering 'Matri Shakti' (women power). He further remarked that such a provision should have been implemented at the very inception of independence; however, due to a lack of political will and the presence of vested interests, this was not possible at the time. Yet today, as the nation advances towards becoming a 'Developed India' under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the necessity to take such a step—dedicated to women's empowerment—was keenly felt, leading to the enactment of this legislation. Its implementation at this juncture is poised to serve as a milestone for the holistic development of women and for enhancing the quality of democracy. He placed special emphasis on the imperative need for the effective implementation of this Act.
At the commencement of the program, Prof. Pranav Kumar, Dean of the School of Social Sciences and Policy, clarified in his welcome and introductory address that genuine transformation across the various dimensions of politics and good governance is attainable only when women not merely participate, but actively assume leadership roles in the processes of policy formulation and decision-making. Citing various examples, he further underscored that women's participation renders governance more transparent, accountable, and responsive. The program coordinator, Prof. Samapika Mahapatra, presented a comprehensive analysis of the social and cultural challenges currently confronting women. She highlighted that traditional mindsets, gender inequality, and societal constraints continue to impede women's full participation today—obstacles that necessitate concrete efforts at both institutional and societal levels to be effectively overcome. Dr. Preeti Anil Khandare, Head of the Department of Historical Studies, outlined the historical background of women's participation, noting that the role of women in Indian society has evolved over time; today, they are establishing a strong presence even in the realm of policy-making. On this occasion, Dr. Poonam presented an analysis of the legal provisions, constitutional basis, and potential implications of the ‘Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023’ (Women's Reservation Act, 2023). Meanwhile, Dr. Amrita Srivastava highlighted the remarkable achievements of women across the fields of education, administration, science, and social sectors. Shedding light on the psychological aspects of women's participation, Dr. Das Ambika Bharti stated that self-confidence, motivation, and social support are indispensable for women to play an active role.
Continuing in this vein, Dr. Jadhav Pratap Singh placed special emphasis on the institutional challenges confronting women—such as inequality of opportunity, limited representation in decision-making processes, and structural barriers—and underscored the necessity of policy reforms to address these challenges. During the program, Dr. Usha Tiwari and Dr. Renu also shared their perspectives, shedding light on various dimensions of women's empowerment. A large number of students present on the occasion participated enthusiastically and engaged in an active dialogue on the subject, thereby further enriching the academic atmosphere of the event.
In the concluding phase of the session, Dr. Firdaus Fatima Rizvi presented a summary of the entire discourse, highlighting the key points and recommendations. She asserted that awareness, institutional support, and social change are absolutely essential for the effective implementation of the Act. The program formally concluded with a vote of thanks delivered by Dr. Parijat Pradhan, who expressed gratitude to all the speakers, participants, and organizers. Dr. Abhay also played a pivotal role in the successful organization of this event. Overall, this discussion session proved to be a robust platform for serious deliberation on the various dimensions of the ‘Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023,’ making it evident that neither inclusive policy-making nor the establishment of true good governance is possible without the active and effective participation of women.
