pages.title: Placement Drive with Kshamtalaya Foundation held at Department of Sociological Studies of CUSB, May 05, 2026
pages.text:
Placement Drive with Kshamtalaya Foundation held at Department of Sociological Studies of CUSB, May 05, 2026
The Department of Sociological Studies of Central University of South Bihar (CUSB), Gaya Ji, organized a Placement Drive in association with Kshamtalaya Foundation for the final-year students of M.A. Sociology and M.S.W. programmes. The Kshamtalaya Foundation, a civil society organization working in the areas of education, livelihoods, and community development, was represented by Mr. Abhishek Tiwari and Mr. Subham Bhakat who interacted with students and presented an overview of the organization’s work and mission. The organization conducted selection process comprising a Pre-Placement Talk, Written Assessment, Group Discussion followed by Interview.  The placement drive was coordinated by Prof. Samapika Mohapatra and Dr. Jitendra Ram, members of the Departmental Placement Cell, and oversaw the entire process from planning to execution. During the occasion, faculty members of the department were also present including Prof. Anil Kumar Singh Jha, Dr. Sanat Kr Sharma, Dr. Haresh Narayan Pandey, Dr. Priya Ranjan, Dr. Parijat Pradhan, and Dr. Ahammedul Kabeer A.P.

pages.title: Two-day geological field excursion for UG-PG Geology students, May 02-03, 2026
pages.text:
Two-day geological field excursion for UG-PG Geology students, May 02-03, 2026
The Department of Geology organized a two-day geological field excursion for students enrolled in the five-year integrated UGPG program under the Lab to Land initiative during May 02-03,2026. This visit marked the first field-based learning experience for the undergraduate students, providing them with practical exposure to geological features in the Gaya Ji region. On the first day, students conducted field observations and geological assessments at Koshma, Sita Kund, Bhindas, Gehlor Valley (Dashrath Manjhi Dwar), Jethian Pass, Rajgir, and the Gulani area. They examined rock formations, identified mineral assemblages, and analyzed structural features and landscape evolution in these locations.
The second day focused on detailed geological exploration of Pretshila, Laal Pahad, Barabar Hills, Nagarjuna Hills, and Brahmayoni Hills. Students engaged in hands-on study of lithology, geomorphological characteristics, and structural geology, enhancing their understanding through direct field investigation. This field excursion proved highly beneficial, enabling students to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world geological settings and develop essential fieldwork skills. The program was coordinated by Dr. Dhirendra Kumar, Assistant Professor, under the supervision of Prof. Prafull Kumar Singh, Head of the Department of Geology. Prof. Singh emphasized the importance of field-based learning in geology, highlighting its critical role in developing observational skills and practical understanding. He also congratulated Dr. Dhirendra Kumar for successfully initiating this field-oriented learning approach for the UG–PG program.

pages.title: EVS students participated in ICSSR Sponsored National Conference at GBU, Greater Noida, April 27-28, 2026
pages.text:
EVS students participated in ICSSR Sponsored National Conference at GBU, Greater Noida, April 27-28, 2026
Students from the Department of Environmental Science at Central University of South Bihar (CUSB), Gaya, including PhD scholars Avinash Dass, Jay Prakash, Nisha, Manisha, Shubham, Jay Prabha, and masters students Shailja, Anamika, and Avinash Jha had been participated actively in the two-day ICSSR-sponsored National Conference titled The Nexus Imperative: Environment, Public Health and Policy for a Sustainable Future, held at Gautam Buddha University, Uttar Pradesh, on April 2728, 2026. Organized by the Department of Environmental Science, the conference cantered on the theme Translating Science into Policy for Healthier Communities and Ecosystems. It brought together students, researchers, academicians, and policymakers from across India, creating a dynamic platform for interdisciplinary dialogue and knowledge exchange. The programme featured keynote lectures, thematic technical sessions, panel discussions, brainstorming interactions, and capacity-building workshops addressing critical intersections of environmental systems, public health, and policy frameworks.
A notable highlight of the conference was the academic leadership and recognition accorded to the department. Prof. Rajesh Kumar Ranjan, Head of the Department of Environmental Science at CUSB, Gaya was invited to serve as a Session Chair, underscoring the institution’s growing academic prominence at the national level. Following this, Prof. Parth Sarthi contributed as an eminent speaker, delivering an insightful discourse on climate change in relation to Indigenous Knowledge Systems, where he emphasized the importance of integrating traditional ecological knowledge with contemporary climate adaptation and mitigation strategies.
The conference also witnessed strong and active student engagement from CUSB, reflecting the department’s commitment to interdisciplinary research and policy-relevant scientific inquiry. Students participated in various technical sessions, presenting their research and contributing to meaningful academic discussions. Their efforts were recognized in the Oral Presentation category, where Shubham secured the Third Prize, and Avinash Dass received a Consolation Prize, marking significant achievements for the department. Overall, the participation and accomplishments of both faculty and students highlight the Department of Environmental Science at CUSB’s continued dedication to academic excellence, research dissemination, and capacity building, while contributing to the broader goal of sustainable and evidence-based environmental governance.

pages.title: Four CUSB Alumnae bagged the prestigious Chief Minister’s Fellowship Scheme of Bihar
pages.text:
Four CUSB Alumnae bagged the prestigious Chief Minister’s Fellowship Scheme of Bihar
The Chief Minister's Fellowship Scheme (CMFS) in Bihar, in partnership with IIM Bodh Gaya, is a two-year program designed for professionals to contribute to governance and development, offering a Post Graduate Certificate in Public Policy and Good Governance. The program places 121 fellows in key government departments with monthly stipends of ₹80,000–₹1,50,000, involving training, mentorship, and on-ground experience.   This Fellowship is a unique, high-impact programme designed for exceptional professionals who aspire to lead social change and co-create the blueprint for a developed Bihar by 2047. This programme moves beyond the traditional classroom. It integrates rigorous academic training from IIM Bodh Gaya with high-stakes practical experience inside the state government. The Fellow will learn the principles of policy and immediately apply them in real-time. Fellows are placed in high-impact offices to support senior decision-makers in policy formulation, implementation, and assessment. This is a rare opportunity to gain first-hand experience in the mechanics of governance. The first of its kind in Bihar, our four alumnae were selected for this programme. They include Bimlesh Bhagat from the Department of Development Studies (2010-12 batch), Shourabh Kumar Singh from the Department of Environment Studies (2016-18 batch), Deepika Kumari from the Department of Development Studies (2019-21 batch) and Neha Kumari from the Department of Sociological Studies (2019-21 batch).

pages.text:
MA Economics student Chandan Kumar Honoured with NPTEL Believer Award
Chandan Kumar, a Master’s student of the Department of Economic Studies and Policy, has been awarded the NPTEL Believer Award at the NPTEL Star Felicitation Award Ceremony 2026, held on March 8, 2026, in Kolkata organised by IIT Kharagpur. He earned this recognition for the July–December 2025 session for successfully completing multiple NPTEL courses with consistent academic performance. The Honourable Vice-Chancellor Prof. K. N. Singh, Head of the Department Prof. Krishnan Chalil, and SWAYAM Coordinator of the Department - Dr. Atish Kumar Dash congratulated him. Faculty members Dr. Abodh Kumar, Dr. Firdaus Fatima Rizvi, Dr. Sanjay Kumar, Dr. Rikil Chyrmang, and Dr. Rajni Kant Ojha also appreciated his achievement.

pages.title: Five-Day Social Work Camp for MSW students at Vikas Bharati in Gumla, Jharkhand, April 17-21,2026
pages.text:
Five-Day Social Work Camp for MSW students at Vikas Bharati in Gumla, Jharkhand, April 17-21,2026
Students pursuing a Master of Social Work (2nd Semester) at the Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) successfully completed a five-day social work camp at Vikas Bharati, located in Bishunpur, Gumla, Jharkhand. Acting on the recommendation of Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameswar Nath Singh and under the supervision of Prof. Vijay Kumar Sharma, Head of the Department of Sociological Studies, the students participated in this camp from April 17 to April 21, 2026. During the camp, other faculty members—Dr. Haresh Narayan Pandey, Dr. Parijat Pradhan, and Dr. Priya Ranjan—also accompanied the students. The objective of this camp, organized as an integral part of the curriculum, was to expose students to rural and tribal communities and to provide them with practical, hands-on experience in understanding development initiatives currently underway at the grassroots level.
During the camp, Mr. Mahendra Bhagat, Joint Secretary of Vikas Bharati, interacted with the CUSB team, providing them with detailed information about the organization, its vision, and the work being undertaken in various sectors such as tribal development, rural development, livelihoods, healthcare, and agriculture. The students also visited the Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) in Bishunpur, where Mr. Mahendra Bhagat, Dr. Brajesh Pandey, Mr. Kaushal Kumar, Mr. Sunil Kumar, and Dr. Nishi Tiwari briefed them extensively on the center's research areas, activities, and various initiatives.
Throughout the camp, prior to participating in various activities, the students were provided with essential guidelines regarding the camp's objectives, ethical conduct, and field-work protocols. The institution operates in diverse sectors—including agriculture, animal husbandry, and horticulture—focusing on areas such as seeds, organic fertilizers (such as *Jivamrit* and *Bijamrit*), various breeds of cattle, sheep, and goats, as well as crops such as wheat, paddy, millet, and mangoes. At the KVK, students also witnessed firsthand several innovative initiatives related to the marketing of products made from millet—such as laddoos, savory mixtures, biscuits, and cakes.
Head of the Department, Prof. Vijay Kumar Sharma, stated that during their visit, the students interacted with members of the local community, observed various development programs, and gained experience in field-based learning. This experience enabled the students to understand rural socio-economic conditions, appreciate the role of non-governmental organizations in advancing development initiatives, and acquire grassroots-level insights.

pages.title: CUSB Agriculture students showcase Innovative Rural Marketing Strategies, April 16, 2026
pages.text:
CUSB Agriculture students showcase Innovative Rural Marketing Strategies, April 16, 2026
Students from the Department of Agriculture at the Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) presented innovative and practical strategies for marketing agricultural products in rural areas, as part of the Agribusiness Management module included in their curriculum. This exhibition was organized by CUSB's Department of Commerce and Business Studies, showcasing creative and practical marketing techniques developed by the students.
The event was conducted under the guidance of Dr. Rajnarayanan S., Associate Professor and Course Module Director. Prof. Avneesh Prakash Singh, Head of the Department of Agriculture, welcomed the faculty members and, while addressing the students, remarked that such exhibitions are immensely helpful in fostering students' practical knowledge and their understanding of real-world scenarios. Dr. Rajnarayanan S. shed detailed light on the various challenges encountered in the marketing of agricultural products—particularly within rural markets—and encouraged the students to develop innovative solutions.
A total of nine student groups participated in the exhibition, demonstrating various unique strategies aimed at enhancing the marketing of agricultural products. The projects were evaluated by Dr. Pawas Kumar, Dr. Pradeep Ram, and research scholar Ms. Shruti, who commended the participants for their efforts and creativity. This exhibition proved to be an effective platform for students to bridge the gap between theoretical studies and practical application within the field of agribusiness.

pages.title: Collaborative UGC-DAE Research grant of approximately Rs 15 Lakhs to Dr. Rohit Ranjan of CUSB
pages.text:
Collaborative UGC-DAE Research grant of approximately Rs 15 Lakhs to Dr. Rohit Ranjan of CUSB
The research proposal of Dr. Rohit Ranjan Shahi of the Department of Physics of Central University of South Bihar (CUSB) has been approved under the UGA-DAE Collaborative research Grant. Under this project of value approximately Rs. 15 lakh, a joint investigation will be performed for the excellent magnetic High entropy materials for advanced applications in modern Electric vehicle, data storage and memory devices. CUSB Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh, Prof. Narendra Kumar Rana, Registrar and other faculty members have congratulated Dr. Shahi and his research team. VC Prof. K. N. Singh said such joint collaborative research will be definitely beneficial for the university and the country. Dean School of Physical and chemical sciences, and other faculty of the department congratulated Dr. Shahi for his achievement.
Dr. Shahi did extensive work on magnetic properties of multi-component alloys in the last five years, and two Ph.D. students completed their thesis on Magnetic High Entropy alloys.  Dr. Shahi dedicated this achievement to his Ph.D. Students Dr. Rajesh Mishra, Mrs. Priyanka Kumari and Mr. Shashikant Mohapatra. Elaborating further Dr. Ranjan said under this project, research will be focused on the magnetic behavior of High Entropy Alloys. New magnetic alloys and their thin films will be searched to minimize the eddy current loss. Transformers are used in each and every electrical and electronic device any small change in the transformer performance can enhance the efficiency of the device in many folds. Moreover, most of the commercial core magnets are made of Rare Earth based elements which are imported from China and Russia. Thus, this project will be able to fulfill the Make-In –India initiative of GOI. Under this collaborative project, the design and development of novel multi-component high entropy magnets will be executed at CUSB and all detailed magnetic measurements will be performed at IUAC Indore.

pages.title: Law Student Sanjeev Kumar became 'Budget Quest' Finalist, got a chance for virtual dialogue with PM Shri Narendra Modi, April 13, 2026
pages.text:
Law Student Sanjeev Kumar became 'Budget Quest' Finalist, got a chance for virtual dialogue with PM Shri Narendra Modi, April 13, 2026
Sanjeev Kumar, a final-year B.A. LL.B. student at the School of Law and Governance, Central University of South Bihar (CUSB), has brought laurels to both the university and the state by securing a spot in the finals of the prestigious 'My Bharat Budget Quest 2026.' Selected from a pool of over 1.2 million participants nationwide, he has now earned the opportunity to engage in a direct virtual dialogue with the Honorable Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi. Congratulating Sanjeev on this achievement, Vice-Chancellor Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh hailed it as a testament to CUSB's academic excellence and social commitment. On this occasion, Registrar Prof. Narendra Kumar Rana—along with NSS Programme Officer Dr. Anil Kumar, Dr. Dev Narayan Singh, and faculty members from various departments—extended their congratulations and best wishes to Sanjeev.
This national-level competition was focused on the Union Budget 2026, aiming to enhance youth participation in policy formulation and align with the vision of a 'Viksit Bharat' (Developed India). Sanjeev's selection underscores his profound understanding of fiscal policy and the grassroots-level challenges facing Bihar. Sanjeev expressed his gratitude to the Nodal Officer of the Pro Bono Club, Dr. Dev Narayan Singh; NSS Programme Officer Dr. Anil Kumar; and Dean Prof. Ashok Kumar for their invaluable guidance.

pages.title: CUSB Law department students Mini Sinha and Ankita Roy won National Pro Bono Competition in Dehradun, April 12, 2026
pages.text:
CUSB Law department students Mini Sinha and Ankita Roy won National Pro Bono Competition in Dehradun, April 12, 2026
Demonstrating excellence in legal service and social commitment, Mini Sinha and Ankita Roy—students of the School of Law and Governance (SLG) at the Central University of South Bihar (CUSB)—secured the top position in the 3rd National Pro Bono Competition held in Dehradun. Hosted at the Dehradun-based UPES University, this prestigious competition saw participation from law students across the country, with the objective of fostering the spirit of pro bono legal services and ensuring equal access to justice. Under the guidance of SLG Dean Prof. Ashok Kumar and the Pro Bono Club's Nodal Officer, Dr. Deo Narayan Singh, Mini Sinha and Ankita Roy outperformed all other participants with their exceptional performance to claim the coveted trophy. Throughout the competition, across various rounds, both students demonstrated a profound understanding of legal aid, community engagement, and innovative methods for providing assistance to marginalized sections of society. The sustained efforts of Nodal Officer Dr. Dev Narayan Singh and Dean Prof. Ashok Kumar played a pivotal role in cultivating a spirit of public service among the students; their guidance was invaluable in shaping the team's preparation and approach for the competition. Following their victory and having secured the top title in Dehradun, the winning team paid a formal visit to the Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Kameshwar Nath Singh. Handing over the winning trophy to the students, Vice-Chancellor Prof. K.N. Singh lauded their achievement and commended the Pro Bono Club for its consistent efforts. He remarked that such accomplishments reflect the university's vision of integrating social responsibility with academic excellence. This success serves as a source of inspiration for other students and highlights the crucial role that pro bono services play in ensuring equal access to justice.
